meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law foundation with local statutes and customary land law elements)

Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER) Plus

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1992 (Cap. 222); Companies (Amendment) Act 2014; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2014 (AML/CFT Act, as amended); Vanuatu Financial Services Commission Act 2014; International Companies (Amendment) Act 2016; Beneficial Ownership Register Regulations (issued under the International Companies Act and AML/CFT framework, effective 2019); AML/CFT Regulations 2015; Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) Directives under the AML/CFT Act; Companies (Beneficial Ownership) (Amendment) Act 2019

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (issued post-registration; pre-incorporation name reservation certificate is registry-generated and does not require notarization)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Registrar of International Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Vanuatu acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention 1961 on 6 February 2002)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Constitutional Documents)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent / applicant company secretary, notarized by authorized Vanuatu notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Vanuatu Ministry of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and External Trade

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of director's passport and residential utility bill (KYC bundle)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country notary public (if not in Vanuatu) or Vanuatu notary for locally executed documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the origin country's competent authority; if non-Hague signatory, full consular legalization via Vanuatu consulate/embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter in favor of the proposed International Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate or private bank where beneficial owner maintains account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, depending on the country of issue

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing for any corporate shareholder/ubo entity (if applicable)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based PEP and sanctions screening as required by the AML/CFT Act 2014 and the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) Directives. The registered agent must screen all directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against (i) the consolidated OFAC SDN list and sectoral sanctions, (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade sanctions list, and (iv) domestic Vanuatu gazetted sanctions and FIU alerts. Screening is required at onboarding, on a rolling monthly basis, and upon any trigger event. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is mandatory for politically exposed persons, which includes immediate family members and close associates; approval of the registered agent's compliance officer or AML/CFT compliance officer is required before accepting a PEP-related engagement. Negative news screening, source-of-funds documentation, and source-of-wealth documentation are required for all non-face-to-face onboarding of the proposed e-commerce International Company.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: VFSC Online Registry System (accessible through the official portal of the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission at www.vfsc.vu; name reservations and company incorporations are generally filed electronically through a licensed registered agent's portal or paper forms to the VFSC Companies Registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The International Companies Act 1992 requires that a company name be distinguishable from names already registered or reserved. Names may be given in English or in any script, provided a Roman-letter transliteration is submitted; statutory official records are maintained in English. The name must not include any word or expression that the Registrar considers unsuited for an International Company; names implying sovereign connection, ethnic or religious exclusivity, or emulating protected statutory bodies are generally prohibited. Bilingual names must be accompanied by notarized transliteration and, where applicable, a certified translation into English.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: National or international development institutions such as 'World Bank', 'IMF', 'UNDP', 'United Nations'
Incorporated (abbreviated as 'Inc.' is acceptable in some cases but may be restricted due to confusion with US-style entities)
Partnership (unless expressly authorized under the International Companies Act)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the VFSC Registrar rejects a proposed name, the applicant (through the licensed registered agent) may submit a formal administrative appeal in writing to the Registrar of International Companies within 21 days of rejection notice. The appeal must state grounds, include a statutory declaration from an authorized official of the applicant, and attach a comparative list of registered names showing distinguishability. The Registrar must issue a decision within 30 days. An adverse final administrative decision may be appealed to the Vanuatu Supreme Court within 30 days of the Registrar's final determination; judicial review is governed by the Judicial Review (Court Procedures) Act 2006. If the initial 30-day reservation expires because of unresolved appeal, the name may be re-reserved for a further 30 days upon payment of the resubmission fee, provided no third party has reserved the identical or confusingly similar name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for this industry with statutory constraints: every International Company must maintain a fixed registered office in Vanuatu, which can be provided by the licensed registered agent's physical address. The physical address is a fully compliant corporate registered office and serves as the statutory address for service of process; the e-commerce business does not need to operate a physical commercial facility in Vanuatu. However, the VFSC and the registered agent may require evidence of a functional business address for the electronic retailing operation in its operational market. Pure virtual-office arrangements are permissible only where the registered agent maintains real physical premises in Port Vila or Luganville, the office hours are publicly indicated, and all statutory records are available at that address. Non-face-to-face e-commerce risk is accepted, but the registered agent must conduct video-verification and EDD to compensate for absence of a physical operational presence in Vanuatu.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For a low-risk standard-tier e-commerce International Company with no physical operations in Vanuatu, the quantified risk of unannounced physical inspection is estimated at 10–15% within the first 24 months of incorporation. The VFSC has powers of inspection under the International Companies Act 1992 and AML/CFT Act 2014; registered agents are subject to periodic compliance inspections, but direct on-site inspections are rarely executed for exclusively foreign e-commerce enterprises. If the company becomes high-volume, receives suspicious transaction reports from payment processors, or is connected to a PEP, inspection likelihood rises materially above 40%.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the International Companies (Fees) Regulations 1992, as amended

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT KYC and UBO verification package for a standard low-risk corporate directorship structure
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed registered agent / corporate services provider

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act [Cap 152] (as amended), ss. 1, 8, 14, 15 and First Schedule (Memorandum and Articles of Association); Vanuatu Financial Services Commission Act [Cap 322] (VFSC administration); Companies (Amendment) Act notifications as consolidated by VFSC Registry practice.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) — Companies Registry, Corporate Affairs Division, Port Vila
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association submitted to the Registrar, together with Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company), executed by each subscriber and countersigned by the licensed Registered Agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement. Authorised capital may be expressed in any currency; subscribed shares may be issued unpaid or credited as fully paid without escrow or bank deposit evidence. Agreed Capital designation election is permitted; paid-up capital evidenced solely by entries in the Register of Members.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the subscriptions of the first shareholders in the number of shares set out in the register of members be and are hereby accepted, the shares be allotted and credited as fully paid, and the issuance be recorded in the register of members; (2) the registered office located at the office of the licensed registered agent in Port Vila, Vanuatu be adopted as the company's registered office; (3) [Director name] be appointed Director and [Secretary name] be appointed Company Secretary and AML Compliance Officer; (4) the authorised share capital be designated as Agreed Capital; (5) any one director be authorised to execute ancillary filings, bank mandates, and payment-rail applications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Agent Engagement and Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC through a VFSC-licensed Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute an engagement letter appointing a VFSC-licensed Registered Agent. Submit two or three proposed company names for clearance; each name must be distinguishable from existing registrations and not misleading or prohibited under the International Companies Act. The agent lodges the name reservation request with the VFSC Registry and confirms availability before drafting constitutional documents.
required_dossiers: Duly executed Registered Agent engagement letter
Name clearance request (Form NR-1)
Certified passport copy of each subscriber
Proof of residential address of each subscriber (utility bill or bank statement, dated within 3 months)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for similarity or prohibited character, an alternative distinctive name is filed within 5 business days; a formal appeal may be lodged with the Registrar under s. 12 of the International Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent with attestation before a notary public in Port Vila
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in the statutory form prescribed by the First Schedule of the International Companies Act. Circulate final proof to subscribers, obtain authorised-signature execution, and have each subscriber's signature notarised. Directors and the company secretary execute consents to act. The registered office consent is obtained from the licensed agent.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (signed)
Notarised signature pages of subscribers
Consent to act as Director for each appointee
Consent to act as Company Secretary
Registered office consent signed by the licensed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry or agent identifies inconsistencies in the execution block, the relevant pages are re-executed and re-notarised before submission; no re-drafting of approved clauses is required where only signature formalities are defective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to VFSC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC Companies Registry (counter in Port Vila or online portal operated by VFSC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form IC-1 together with the signed Memorandum and Articles of Association, consents, and proof of payment of the USD 300 government filing fee. The Registered Agent verifies that all exhibits are paginated and cross-referenced. VFSC officers check compliance with capital, name, subscriber, and officer requirements before allocating a company registration number.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation of International Company)
Signed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consents to act of directors and secretary
Registered agent certificate of acceptance of office
VFSC filing fee remittance advice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VFSC issues a query or section 16 notice, respond in writing within 14 days, correct the noted deficiency, pay any shortfall fee, and resubmit the amended page; refusal may be appealed to the VFSC Registrar whose decision is subject to judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfaction of filing requirements, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation stating the company name, registration number, and date of incorporation. The Registered Agent collects the certificate, verifies details against the application, and provides a certified copy to the company. The certificate is conclusive evidence of incorporation and date of commencement.
required_dossiers: VFSC filed application reference number
VFSC receipt of incorporation fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical error in name, number, or date, the Registered Agent files a written correction request under s. 14(5) and the Registrar reissues the certificate without re-incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Governance Pack and Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors acting by written resolution at the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting by written resolution in lieu of meeting. Adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution covering share subscription, registered office, and officer appointments. Establish statutory registers (members, directors, charges, and minutes), issue share certificates to subscribers, and deliver the registered office copy of registers to the licensed agent in compliance with the International Companies Act.
required_dossiers: First Board written resolution
Register of Members and Register of Directors templates
Share certificates executed under seal
AML/CFT CDD file and risk assessment for e-commerce operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum or execution deficiencies are identified, a ratifying unanimous written resolution is circulated to all directors and filed in the minutes book; third-party reliance is protected by the certificate of incorporation unless the defect is fraudulent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC-licensed commercial banks in Vanuatu and payment processors (Stripe, PayPal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the incorporation kit to a Vanuatu-licensed bank for corporate account opening, including the certificate, constitutional documents, and first board resolution. For payment rails, complete Stripe and PayPal merchant onboarding using the company legal name, certificate of incorporation, website/storefront URL, and beneficial owner information, with transaction-velocity and refund-policy disclosures appropriate for pet-supplies retail.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (certified copy)
Memorandum and Articles of Association
First Board Resolution authorising bank and payment accounts
Director KYC documents (passport, residential proof, bank reference)
E-commerce storefront URL and pro-forma invoice for underwriting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or processor queries the application, supply a source-of-funds declaration and corporate structure chart; invoke the processor's appeal channel or route the account through an alternative acquiring bank approved by VFSC; no change of incorporation is required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial licensing board governs electronic retail of pet supplies; the IC is an offshore, non-resident company that does not carry on local business. Any physical import of goods into Vanuatu is handled by the Vanuatu Customs Division, Department of Customs and Inland Revenue.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No VFSC operating licence or manufacturing permit is required. The IC is exempt from the Business Licence Act because it conducts only non-resident e-commerce activities and maintains no trading presence in Vanuatu; no tourism, financial, or retail licence applies to the ISIC 4791 scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Vanuatu Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC), Ministry of Climate Change
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category C (no physical installation, manufacturing, or emissions). No EIA report, environmental registration, or environmental monitoring condition is required for a pure e-commerce retail activity; an EIA would arise only if warehousing or fulfilment infrastructure were established onshore.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable at formation. If bonded warehousing or repacking operations are later added, DEPC Waste Management Regulations require segregation of packaging waste, prohibition of open burning, disposal through authorised contractors, and compliance with the Vanuatu Water and Sanitation Act discharge thresholds for any washwater or leaching from returned electronics/pet devices.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable — no physical premises in Vanuatu. If a retail warehouse, repacking room, or fulfilment centre is subsequently leased, clearance under the Vanuatu National Fire Service Act (Cap 176), structural approval under the National Building Code, and workplace health certification under the Health and Safety at Work Act would be required before occupancy and first use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) – International Companies Registry; Vanuatu Customs and Inland Revenue Department (CIRD) has only residual customs duty administration powers (no direct tax or VAT competency)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities incorporating an International Company (IC) must engage a VFSC-licensed registered agent to file the Incorporation Application under the International Companies Act, Chap. 222. No separate TIN/VAT ID is issued because Vanuatu levies no income tax, corporation tax, or consumption tax. The VFSC Certificate of Incorporation, together with the registered agent appointment, constitutes the sole statutory tax-identity instrument, supplemented by any goodwill or regulatory references from the VFSC company search upon request.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone – Inward investment vehicle wholly exempt from all national taxes, capital gains taxes, and stamp duties by virtue of Part 12 of the International Companies Act, Chap. 222; no territorial or residency-based taxation trigger exists for ICs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None – Vanuatu recognizes no check-the-box entity classification regime, no hybrid mismatch election, and no utilization of tax treaty attributes; the IC status is a self-executing full tax immunity, with no elective downgrade into a taxable corporate vehicle domestically.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST regime – Vanuatu operates only a limited customs import duty system under the Customs Act [Cap. 233]; exports and offshore services are completely outside the indirect tax perimeter
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A – there is no indirect tax registration threshold, no fiscal numbering for VAT, and no dealer registration requirement; ICs importing physical goods into Vanuatu for local delivery would trigger standard customs duties (typically 8%–15% ad valorem depending on tariff classification, plus possible stamp duty on customs entries), but pure e-commerce export sales from Vanuatu or fulfilment outside Vanuatu incur zero indirect tax obligations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None – Vanuatu has no e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API integration with tax administration, or digital stamping/marking requirement for invoices; the CIRD maintains a manual customs electronic data interchange (ASYCUDA) solely for import goods declaration, not for sales invoices or VAT clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable – because no VAT/GST is levied in Vanuatu, the 0% export VAT concept does not exist; export sales of pet supplies and related goods from (or originated in) Vanuatu by an IC are wholly outside any indirect tax charge, with no requirement to substantiate a zero rate and no refund procedure to invoke.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration (if goods physically consigned from Vanuatu and subject to export documentation under the Customs Act [Cap. 233])
Commercial invoice with HS tariff classification and shipment terms
Bill of Lading or House Air Waybill evidencing cross-border dispatch
Certificate of origin (only where requested by the destination jurisdiction or trade agreement; no Vanuatu zero-rating purpose)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT clawback or retrospective export zero-rating adjustment is applicable as Vanuatu imposes no indirect tax on exports. However, the VFSC may impose administrative fines (up to VT 1,000,000), cancellation of the IC licence, and deregistration for the filing of false declarations concerning offshore status, registered office, or agent details under the International Companies Act. For customs purposes, under-declaration or misdescription of goods in an import entry triggers civil penalties up to double the duty short-paid and potential criminal forfeiture under the Customs Act. E-commerce merchants should also maintain in-country agent records and auditable transaction flow evidence to demonstrate that the IC is not engaged in prohibited local trading, which would otherwise violate the IC's exemption terms.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV) under the Currency Act, the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu Act and the Exchange Control Act [Cap 56]; banking licensing and AML/CFT supervision are jointly administered by the RBV and the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vanuatu maintains a fully open and unrestricted exchange-control regime; current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible and no RBV approval, exchange-control licence, or profit-repatriation permit is required for cross-border remittances. The national currency is the Vatu (VUV), which is administered on a managed-float basis against a trade-weighted currency basket. Profit and capital remittances by an International Company are unhindered by income tax, capital gains tax, or dividend withholding tax because Vanuatu imposes none of those taxes; the material constraints are therefore operational rather than regulatory, namely limited offshore VUV liquidity, increased KYC/EDD requirements imposed by understaffed compliance teams, and correspondent-bank documentation demands for USD/AUD clearing. E-commerce settlement is best conducted entirely in USD to eliminate convertibility friction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None statutorily applicable. Vanuatu imposes no surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline for export receipts. Exporters, including electronic retailers of pet supplies and devices, may retain 100% of foreign-currency proceeds in Foreign Currency Accounts (FCAs) at licensed commercial banks and may freely deploy those funds for imports or treasury purposes. In practice the RBV requires commercial banks to apply AML screening to inward SWIFT credits and to record purpose-of-remittance data; the recommended treasury policy for the Stage 4 mandate is to invoice in USD via Stripe/PayPal, settle net proceeds into a USD FCA, and defer any VUV or AUD conversion until discrete local expenditure is scheduled.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account (USD/AUD/VUV) with D2C merchant-settlement wallets; can host Capital Escrow Account for subscribed paid-up capital and intercompany loan conduit.
Operational multi-currency account (USD/AUD/VUV/PGK) with established USD correspondent clearing via BSP Group Pacific network; suitable as the primary settlement account for PSP payouts.
Operational VUV/AUD account with limited USD direct-clearing capability; appropriate for local payroll and VAT/statutory payments only.
Operational multi-currency account (EUR/USD/AUD/VUV) with a strong European correspondent network; useful for EU-supplier settlement and euro-denominated inventory replenishment.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate as a settlement-enabler but low as a replacement for a Vanuatu licensed bank account. Vanuatu has no domestic Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing regime; foreign EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, and Stripe Treasury are not recognised deposit-takers by the RBV and cannot hold clearing accounts in the national payments system. Legal constraints require that a foreign EMI, if used, holds a valid e-money/PSP authorisation in its home jurisdiction, provides a complete transaction audit trail, and causes all merchant settlement to be swept via SWIFT to the IC's physical USD account at ANZ or BSP within strict timelines; domestic banks will refuse to perpetuate a 'nested' account where funds remain offshore beyond 60 days, citing correspondent de-risking. Stripe and PayPal are treated as unregulated collection PSPs and are permissible for front-end D2C card capture; the recommended architecture is Stripe/PayPal payout to BSP or ANZ USD FCA, then scheduled MT103 wires for supplier and logistics disbursement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence at a Vanuatu branch is not mandatory for the International Company's directors or shareholders; remote opening is permitted and is the standard onboarding path. Each tier-1 bank requires the following remotely executable package: (i) newly issued original or notarised Certificates of Incorporation/Continuation, Good Standing from VFSC, Memorandum & Articles, Register of Directors and Shareholders, and a copy of the Beneficial Ownership Return; (ii) a live video interview conducted by the bank's Money Laundering Reporting Officer covering business model, source of funds, expected volume, and counterparty jurisdictions; (iii) bank introduction letters from the source-country bank of each UBO, dated within 90 days; and (iv) a signed waiver confirming no nominee opacity. In practice, at least one of the IC's directors or its licensed registered agent must engage a Port Vila corporate services firm to courier the physical KYC bundle and execute the local 'Client Acceptance Sign-off', but no director need appear personally.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt offshore International Company with zero domestic substance and no tax filing evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: VFSC Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing; registered agent and registered office declaration; four-page substance memo describing the e-commerce operating model (supplier countries, logistics chain, web storefront, customer base); reviewed or audit-prepared financial statements of the operating affiliate; attestation that no physical business presence or local board operations exist in Vanuatu.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency merchant settlement velocity and chargeback volatility originating from Stripe/PayPal PSP accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rolling three-month Stripe and PayPal merchant statements or dashboard exports; chargeback and refund ratio reports; signed PSP merchant agreements containing the settlement-sweep clause; refund policy and customer-support protocol; field-level evidence that the PSP account is owned by the IC and not a third-party aggregator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owners domiciled in jurisdictions perceived as higher-risk or without a substantive banking relationship.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies and current residential proof of all natural-person UBOs; bank reference letter and source-of-wealth statement from each UBO's principal resident bank; copies of any relevant trust deeds or nominee declarations; an organisational chart demonstrating the controls over the IC and the operating affiliate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee-director screen or incomplete beneficial-ownership disclosure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed VFSC Beneficial Ownership Return under the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2019; certified share ledger showing natural persons as final UBOs; executed nominee resignation covenants; confirmation letter from the licensed registered agent corroborating the beneficial ownership register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: 'Ghost e-commerce' red flag: mismatch between domain ownership, physical fulfilment, and claimed operational capacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ICANN domain registration records; website and marketplace listings for pet supplies/devices; supplier purchase orders and product certificates; 3PL warehouse agreements and shipping manifests; live administrative access to PSP dashboard demonstrated under the video interview.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: the shareholder or parent entity wires paid-up capital or an intercompany shareholder loan from its own bank account to the IC's USD settlement account at ANZ or BSP using SWIFT MT103 with OFAC-screened messaging. Vanuatu imposes no central-bank approval and no fixed purpose-code table for inbound remittances; the remittance must include a free-text reason-for-payment such as 'SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - IC REG NO VU_IC' or 'INTERCOMPANY LOAN - INV/LOAN NO.', and the bank's reconciliation team will match the MT103 field 70 against a board resolution and signed capital-escrow instruction letter. For operational e-commerce liquidity, Stripe/PayPal settlement arrives via international ACH/SWIFT into the same USD FCA in sweeps; all inward credits are screened by the bank on a positive-pay reconciliation basis. Third-party deposits are prohibited: the remitter must be a named shareholder or lender, and the supporting file must include the board resolution authorising the capital, the remitter's certified identity documents, and proof of source of funds for any single credit exceeding USD 100,000, which automatically triggers enhanced due diligence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 corporate wires from the IC's USD FCA to supplier accounts in China, the United States, and the European Union, each wire carrying the invoice reference and a clear remittance instruction ('PET SUPPLY IMPORT / INVOICE NO.') to avoid trade-description flagging; (2) commercial sight letters of credit, confined to bulk periodic purchases of pet-care devices exceeding approximately USD 25,000 per shipment and issued with confirmation from a correspondent negotiating bank because the local LC book is thin; (3) host-to-host or SWIFT FileAct batched payment files for recurring logistics and fulfilment suppliers; and (4) PSP-initiated payouts (e.g., Stripe Treasury, PayPal MassPay) only as a fallback, subject to the 60-day nesting rule noted above. For local VUV disbursements, the RBV-operated Vanuatu Automated Transfer System (VATS) is the domestic clearing rail; however, the Stage 4 treasury policy is to remain fully USD-denominated and to execute any required VUV conversion at the same domestic bank with a three-day booking window to preserve margin.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/VUV outright forward contracts (up to 12 months) executed with ANZ or BSP under a standard corporate master FX confirmation, supported by underlying trade or expense documentation for RBV audit purposes.

AUD/USD and EUR/USD cross-currency swaps or rollover structures via the bank's own risk book, permitted only above a practical notional of USD 5 million and thus normally unavailable to a small e-commerce IC; natural currency matching is preferred.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on VUV are not bankable because an offshore VUV NDF market does not exist; a USD-based NDF on AUD or EUR for procurement hedging is permissible only through an FCA-protected clearing line with full disclosure to VFSC and the domestic bank.

Vanilla call/put options and structured swap collars are not permissible for an unlicensed International Company without a VFSC investment-dealer or financial-licence extension; the standard prudent policy for this asset-light e-commerce model is multi-currency FCA matching (USD invoicing, USD supplier payout) with strict 10-day FX budgeting and no speculative derivative exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Renewal Declaration for International Company License
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) — International Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation date; filing due annually on or before the date of incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of approximately 10% of the due fee; continued non-payment for a defined period results in administrative dissolution and removal from the International Companies Register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Registered Agent and Registered Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) through licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with annual government renewal; due annually by incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a licensed registered agent and registered office in Vanuatu triggers VFSC compliance action, late renewal penalties, and potential administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) via registered agent records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No separate fixed annual filing date; updated with the annual renewal cycle and upon any change in ultimate beneficial ownership during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with beneficial ownership record-keeping obligations may result in monetary penalties imposed by VFSC and restrictions on corporate activities

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit for Vanuatu International Companies absent a VFSC license, public offering, or specific shareholder resolution requiring audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Companies Act accounting requirements; no prescribed IFRS or Local GAAP filing obligation; books and records must be sufficient to evidence transactions and financial position

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Vanuatu International Companies must maintain current beneficial ownership records at the registered office. Registered agents must obtain and verify beneficial ownership information at commencement and whenever a shareholding transfer occurs. Annual confirmation with the registered agent is required as part of the annual renewal process; the company must disclose any changes to the beneficial ownership identity or percentage.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 – 2,000 (only if voluntarily audited or imposed by a contracted third party)

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 0% — Vanuatu imposes no corporate income tax; International Companies are wholly tax-exempt under s. 8 of the International Companies Act [Cap. 222].
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Nil statutory taxes: zero corporate income tax, zero withholding tax, zero capital gains tax, zero GST/VAT (VAT reform bills have not been enacted). The only annual fiscal charge is the VFSC annual registration/renewal fee for the International Company.
